sprint: Maintenance Sprint 8 — reactive research (7-week gym layoff detected)

facts.fact: Maximal strength shows trivial losses (g < 0.2) for up to 28 days of training cessation; losses accelerate after ~1 month
facts.practical_application: A 2-4 week break costs almost nothing in strength; don't panic-restart
facts.relevance_to_achyut: High — 7-week layoff exceeds grace period but muscle memory applies

facts.fact: Strength endurance (high-rep performance) is lost faster than maximal strength because metabolic conditioning (mitochondria, capillaries, enzymes, blood volume) de-adapts faster than contractile tissue
facts.practical_application: Expect high-rep sets to feel disproportionately hard when returning
facts.relevance_to_achyut: High — his program is 3x10-12 rep-range work

facts.fact: Early muscle 'flatness' during a layoff is glycogen, water/edema, and blood flow loss — not actual contractile protein loss
facts.practical_application: Don't judge muscle loss by the mirror in the first weeks off

facts.fact: Whole-muscle size trends toward baseline after 7-20 weeks of cessation, but muscle fiber cross-sectional area is preserved far better — true tissue loss is slower than whole-muscle measures imply
facts.practical_application: A 7-week layoff likely caused only modest true muscle loss

facts.fact: Older adults (65+) lose strength ~2x faster during detraining (g=0.76 vs g=0.31 in younger adults); younger adults get a ~1-month grace period
facts.practical_application: Age matters: 20-somethings retain gains much longer
facts.relevance_to_achyut: High — falls in protected younger group

facts.fact: Muscle memory is real and cellular: myonuclei added during prior training survive detraining (myonuclear permanence), epigenetic methylation changes persist (Seaborne 2018), and anabolic signaling resensitizes after a break
facts.practical_application: Regaining lost muscle is genuinely faster than building it the first time
facts.relevance_to_achyut: Very high — core reason the comeback will be fast

facts.fact: Time to regain lost strength/muscle is roughly half the layoff duration (range 1/3 to 2/3)
facts.practical_application: 7 weeks off → expect ~3-5 weeks back to previous numbers

facts.fact: Periodic 3-week breaks do not reduce long-term gains: cyclical 6wk-on/3wk-off training produced identical 6-month strength and hypertrophy gains vs continuous training
facts.relevance_to_achyut: Moderate — reduces guilt about time off

facts.fact: Young adults can maintain muscle and strength for months on just 1/9th of their previous training volume; even one set per exercise suffices
facts.practical_application: One 30-45 min bodyweight session per week preserves most gains during layoff

facts.fact: During no-training periods, hold protein at ~1.3-1.4 g/kg LEAN mass and calories near maintenance; extra protein or supplements do NOT retain muscle without training stimulus
facts.practical_application: Moderate protein + maintenance calories during breaks

facts.fact: Complete immobilization/bed rest loses strength >1% per day and muscle ~0.5% per day — an order of magnitude worse than normal detraining
facts.practical_application: Distinguish 'not going to gym' from 'can't move' scenarios

facts.fact: Week 1 back: perform your normal program (same exercises, sets, reps) at ~1/3 of pre-layoff loads — a single light session dramatically attenuates DOMS and damage markers on ramp-up
facts.practical_application: Restart THE-PLAN.md Day A/B/C at ~33% loads to prevent crippling soreness
facts.relevance_to_achyut: Very high — this is his week 1

facts.fact: Week 2 back: autoregulate at 5+ RIR on first set, 3-4 RIR on final set; injury risk is elevated when re-introducing intense training after layoff
facts.practical_application: Challenging but not hard; don't test limits in week 2

facts.fact: Weeks 3+: weekly load increase = (pre-layoff weight − current weight) ÷ (recovery weeks − 1); when weekly progression stalls, retraining is done
facts.practical_application: Quantified ramp back to July numbers in ~4-6 weekly jumps

facts.fact: Layoffs <1 month = simple 20% deload then resume; >1 year = treat as beginner with standard linear progression; avoid fast strength regain on low volume while tendons stay deconditioned
facts.practical_application: 7-week layoff sits between: use the 1/3-loads week 1 + halved-duration ramp
